judge_assessment.explanation: The claim is exact for all five problems. Problem 4 says 'Put a dot on 4/6 and label it P' and verify.json id 4 checks only the simpler name 2/3; problem 5 says 'Put a dot on 8/8' and id 5 checks only the whole number 1; problem 6 says 'Mark 2/3 on the top line and 2/4 on the bottom line' and id 6 is a single compare relation; problem 7 says 'Mark 5/8 on it. Then mark 3/4 on the same line' and id 7 is a single compare relation; problem 9 says 'Put a dot on 5/3 and label it E' and id 9 checks only the 2/3 distance past 1. Seven plotted points in total, none verified and none marked manual, on a worksheet whose declared focus is placing fractions on number lines. SKILL.md itself lists constructions under manual, so this is a departure from the skill's own rule and not merely an unstated gap. The judge is also right that problem 10 is honestly manual and that the fraction values are all correct (1/2, 3/4, 2/3, 2/3, 1, >, <, 3/2, 2/3). One further defect the judge did not report: the Quick Answers bank prints '6. —' and '7. —' for the two verified relations, so the answer key delivers no answer at all for the two comparison problems.

strengths_to_preserve: The count-the-parts-not-the-ticks misconception is engineered into the checks, not just mentioned: problem 2 carries a trap expression a/(b+1) for a child who counts the five tick marks on a fourths line, problem 3 carries (b-a)/b for counting backwards from the point, and problem 8 carries a/(b+2) for reading a 0-to-2 line as if it stopped at 1. The study guide's watch-out closes with the same rule ('a line cut into fourths has five tick marks').

The ramp off the unit interval is well built: problems 1-7 stay inside 0 to 1, problem 8 introduces a line running to 2 in halves, and problem 9 asks not for the point's name but for how far past 1 it sits - encoded honestly as a/b - 1 rather than as the fraction itself. That is a real conceptual step, not a harder number.

Problem 10 is correctly typed manual with a `desc` that tells the reviewer what a right answer must contain (a larger denominator makes a smaller unit fraction), which is exactly the disclosure the other five construction items are missing.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md tells the author to reframe error-analysis items 'via the ordinary types' and, a few lines later, to use manual for 'any explanation/reasoning answer'. Nothing states that an item doing both needs both entries, and no gate enforces it, so the explanation slot is dropped and the sheet reports zero manual items.
evidence: worksheet problems 4, 5, 6, 7 and 9 all instruct the student to mark or label a point on a printed number line; verify.json's only manual entry is id 10.
SKILL.md's manual list already names 'graph sketches ... constructions', so the guidance exists but nothing enforces it - the coverage gate is satisfied by the scalar entry that shares the id.

root_causes.description: The coverage gate is defined per problem id, not per printed response. verify.py fails only when some id in 1..problem_count has no entry at all, so a problem that prints several required responses is fully satisfied by one scalar check, and both the gate log and the delivery message then describe the sheet as completely verified.
evidence: worksheet problem 4 prints a plotted point AND a simplified-name answer; id 4 has one entry.
worksheet problems 6 and 7 each print two plotted points AND a relation symbol; ids 6 and 7 have one entry each.
worksheet problem 9 prints a labelled point AND a distance; id 9 has one entry.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies string expected values and falls back to the em-dash on failure, so relation answers ('<', '>', '=') from compare checks can never appear in the Quick Answers bank.
evidence: verify.json ids 6 and 7 have "expected": ">" and "<"; the compiled answer_key.pdf Quick Answers block prints '6. —' and '7. —'.
The same block prints '10. —' for the genuinely manual item, so a grader cannot distinguish 'see the worked solution' from 'a human must read this'.

improvements.title: Require a paired manual entry for every explain / name-the-error / mark-it response
improvements.proposed_change: SKILL.md carries two rules that pull in opposite directions: the reframing paragraph says error analysis should be encoded 'via the ordinary types - the planted wrong result is checkably wrong and the correction checkably right', while the paragraph eight lines later says to use manual for 'any explanation/reasoning answer'. Authors resolve that by encoding only the numeric correction and dropping the explanation slot. Rewrite the reframing paragraph to state the pairing explicitly: an error-analysis or model-completion item that ALSO prints an explain / name-the-error / circle / cross-out / draw / label slot needs BOTH the typed check for the correction AND a manual entry for that slot under the same id (the curr-088 and curr-100 verify files in this same shard are the worked pattern). Back it with the slot gate so the rule is mechanical, not advisory. Here the five plotted-point constructions in problems 4, 5, 6, 7 and 9 each need a manual entry alongside their scalar check, mirroring what id 10 already does correctly on this same sheet.
improvements.regression_test: Extend tests/check_answer_slots.py with a fixture whose problem stem contains an imperative open-response verb ('Explain in one sentence', 'Circle', 'Draw', 'Label', 'Cross out', 'Which measurement did ... actually find?') and whose verify.json entry for that id is a bare eval. The gate must exit 1 demanding a paired {"type": "manual"} entry. The same fixture passes once the manual entry is added. Today it passes in both states, so the test fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The build's manual-item count becomes trustworthy: exit 2 and the 'flagged manual-review items' banner appear whenever a sheet asks a child to explain, mark or draw something, instead of the build reporting all-green on unreviewed reasoning.
improvements.risk: More sheets exit 2 rather than 0, which looks like a regression on dashboards that treat exit 0 as success. That is the intended trust signal; document it in the build-driver section of SKILL.md so exit 2 is not read as a failure.

improvements.title: Make verification coverage per printed response slot, not per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: verify.py's coverage gate currently passes as soon as every id in 1..problem_count carries one entry (scripts/verify.py, the `missing = [i for i in range(1, problem_count + 1) if i not in ids]` check). Replace that with a slot-level contract: add a build gate that counts the response slots a problem actually prints (each \ansline/\answerline/\ansblank, each \underline{} write-on rule in a stem, each lettered part (a)/(b)/(c), each row of a fill-in table or partially blank sequence) and fails the build unless that id declares at least as many verify entries. Add the matching rule to SKILL.md's JSON-format paragraph, which today only says 'every problem id 1..N has at least one check'. Problems 4, 6, 7 and 9 each print a construction plus a written answer against one declared check.
improvements.regression_test: Add tests/check_answer_slots.py plus a fixture pair under tests/fixtures/: a worksheet .tex whose problem 1 prints two response slots (an inline \underline{} line inside the stem and \problem's automatic answer blank) and a verify.json carrying a single scalar entry for id 1. The gate must exit 1 naming 'problem 1 prints 2 response slots but declares 1 check'. Today build.sh runs that fixture green, so the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the dominant hard-failure class in this shard: a worksheet can no longer print several required responses per problem while reporting itself fully verified.
improvements.risk: Slot counting is a heuristic over LaTeX and prose, so it will over-count on stems that use \underline for emphasis. Keep it a fail-with-named-slot gate (never a silent skip) and allow an explicit per-problem "slots" override in the verify JSON so a genuine one-slot problem can declare that rather than being blocked.

improvements.title: Render compare/relation answers in the Quick Answers bank instead of an em-dash
improvements.proposed_change: scripts/render_quick_answers.py::_fmt sends every string `expected` through sympy.sympify and falls back to '---' on SympifyError. The relation answers a `compare` check with "order": "relation" produces ("<", ">", "=") never parse, so a fully verified relation always prints as '---' - the same glyph the bank uses for a manual-only id, which tells a grader 'see solution' when the verified answer is known. Special-case the three relation tokens before the sympify attempt and emit $<$, $>$, $=$; for an id whose entries mix a relation with values, join them (e.g. '439 $<$ 493'). This sheet prints '6. —' and '7. —' for two verified relations, next to a '10. —' that legitimately means manual - so the same glyph carries two incompatible meanings in one bank.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_render_quick_answers.py add a verify fixture containing {"id": 1, "type": "compare", "values": ["400+30+9", "493"], "order": "relation", "expected": "<"} and assert the generated bank line for id 1 contains '$<$' and not '---'. It fails today (_fmt('<') returns '---') and passes after the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: Every comparison problem - a whole facet in the grade 2-3 place-value and fraction topics - gets a real at-a-glance answer instead of a blank, and the em-dash goes back to meaning only 'manual'.
improvements.risk: Low. The change is confined to one formatting helper; the '---' fallback stays for genuinely unrenderable values.

case_summary: Mathematically this sheet is clean: every fraction location, equivalence and comparison reproduces independently, the number lines render legibly, the traps target the count-the-ticks error precisely, and problem 10 is honestly typed manual with reviewer criteria. The rejection is narrow and correct. The worksheet's declared focus is PLACING fractions on number lines, and the five items that ask a child to place and label a point (4, 5, 6, 7, 9) have their constructions covered by nothing - the scalar entry that shares each id verifies the written answer, not the mark on the line, and no manual entry discloses that a human must look. SKILL.md already says constructions are manual; what is missing is a gate that enforces it. A second, unreported defect: the Quick Answers bank prints an em-dash for both verified comparison relations.
